history.dynasty: Yadava-period saint tradition; temple structure is later (trust management since the 1950 Charity Trust Act)
history.period: Samadhi traditionally dated to Shaka 1219 (1297 CE) - local sources write '1219', i.e. the Shaka year
history.summary: Sant Nivruttinath was the elder brother and guru of Sant Dnyaneshwar, the central figure of the Marathi bhakti (Warkari) tradition. After his parents' death he was initiated into the Nath tradition by Gahaninath in a cave on Anjani mountain near Tryambakeshwar; he in turn initiated Dnyaneshwar. After Dnyaneshwar's samadhi at Alandi, Nivruttinath set out on pilgrimage with his sister Muktabai, lost her in a thunderstorm, and returned to Trimbakeshwar where he took samadhi - traditionally a 'live samadhi' dated to Shaka 1219 (= 1297 CE; some English sources render it as '1219' without the era, others cite ~1297 CE). The samadhi temple at Trimbakeshwar is a major Nath-panth and Warkari pilgrimage centre; disciples of Changdev Maharaj traditionally visited it annually. Management ran through the Gosavi priest family until the 1950 Charity Trust Act; after a 25-year legal suit a 13-member board (nine devotees, three Gosavi family members, one municipal representative) was formed in 2015.

name: Sant Nivruttinath Maharaj Samadhi Mandir
town_description: Trimbak (Trimbakeshwar) is an ancient pilgrim town in Nashik district at the foot of the Brahmagiri hills of the Sahyadris, about 28 km from Nashik city. It is dominated by the Jyotirlinga temple and the Kushavarta kund, believed to be the source of the Godavari river. Beyond Shiva worship, it is the first and oldest centre of the Warkari sampradaya through the Nivruttinath samadhi, and a major ritual town for ancestral rites.

travel.road: Trimbak is approx. 28 km from Nashik city (NH160) with frequent MSRTC buses; the samadhi mandir stands near the Trimbakeshwar temple at the town's religious core.

visitor_information.best_time: November to March for weather. January (Pausha) for the samadhi festival; June-July for the palkhi season.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 5:00 AM-10:00 PM daily (verify). No entry ticket reported; 1-2 hours suffices. Respect local custom - avoid meat, tobacco and alcohol on the premises.
